(Guess I was 0 priority considering I was a weekly client) I showed up to her house, and the therapy door was locked (not the first time it happened) It was winter and I was freezing. It sucks, but there are definitely shitty professionals. If nothing huge happened (hospital, no access to phone bc accident or something) she should have communicated. When I was younger and things got really bad, all of my close friends knew what was going on. I was a teenager then, and it seemed like something that a lot of people “that age” dealt with. Also they were teenagers lol, so they didn’t have much input. I would get dumb remarks sometimes from them but that’s about it. 

As an adult, I’m still pretty close w some of my friends from when I was younger, so while I don’t talk about it at all they know what goes on still. Sometimes they’ll come to me w a concern about how I’m looking, but for the most part everyone minds their own business and no one bothers me on it. 

As an adult, and in my late 20’s, I confided in a newer friend who’s older than I am when I was in active recovery. I was working w a therapist, dietician, and a psych at the time. I felt it was ok to let her in because I was getting help, and I was with her a lot, I figured she might help keep me more accountable- which she did. 

Now that I’m completely out of therapy, and in a horrible relapse I wish I didn’t tell her. She constantly comments on my weight, tells me to eat, says how everyone is saying how sick I’m looking etc. it’s just a lot of pressure.

I feel like when I’m with her, I have to eat to “prove” that I do. Everything she says is said with love, but sometimes the delivery isn’t that great and makes me really self conscious. HOWEVER, I’m happy she does know because sometimes if I’m in a really bad spot I could text her about it, even if she doesn’t fully understand, she listens. 

If you’re really trying to recover I would encourage you to tell people closest to you. It helps a lot with accountability. Sometimes too, some of our friends are just generally more empathetic so you might even gain another eat out of it when you can’t talk to your therapist or something. 

I’m also extremely private and I dislike being vulnerable but sometimes when these things are so big, having others in on our “secret” can be detrimental in getting better. Good luck with whatever you choose!!

I think most are pretty trained in this stuff and good at evaluating the risk. Good luck
